correctness.rationale: The normalized block-row projector and trace objective are derived explicitly, and a rank-matched block diagonal projector family is used rather than arbitrary symmetric data. Every cyclotomic pole is generically simple and uncanceled. A two-block independent coefficient-variation argument makes the universal derivative incidence smooth and hence generic roots simple; a separate two-equation incidence excludes cut-locus roots. Riemann–Hurwitz forces the sharp count and Zariski openness transfers it to general projector data. The exact SymPy verifier checks five genuine projector witnesses. The proof handles all n_i>=2, d>=2 including shared poles, and finite checks are not treated as proof.

originality.rationale: The October 2026 primary paper establishes the ED count for the same scroll ruling curves with unrestricted symmetric matrices, but Section 4 defines GD separately and does not identify the GD count for unbalanced scrolls. Related mathematical findings contain the balanced GD case, an ED stationary-numerator discriminant, and cut-locus monodromy; none implies nonloss of critical points for arbitrary unbalanced rank-matched projector data. Targeted published-result searches for scroll ruling GD, unbalanced poles, cyclotomic lcm and rank-matched projectors returned no matching claim. The distinction is material because projectors form a proper algebraic subvariety of symmetric data, and count can drop on special data families. Historical completeness of all older equivalent terminology remains provisional.

value.rationale: The GD degree is a natural enumerative distance-complexity invariant for an algebraic model inside a Grassmannian. The exact all-parameter formula settles its behavior for the full family of rational-normal-scroll ruling curves, including unequal block sizes and nontrivial cyclotomic overlap; equality is not automatic for arbitrary Grassmannian subvarieties, as the motivating paper's GD/ED contrasts demonstrate. The proof isolates why the constraint to genuine idempotent projectors produces no critical-point loss, a structural fact beyond numerical restatement of ED.
